I have called repeatedly throughout the day, and the call either rings out or ends automatically. This isn’t a one-off issue—mornings are no better when you actually need an appointment. It’s now half past one in the afternoon, and still no answer. If patients are expected to respond promptly, the practice needs to be accessible. At this point, it’s genuinely frustrating and unacceptable. What exactly does it take to get through to someone?

Thank you for your response.

I appreciate the explanation regarding staffing issues and the previous callback problem.

However, I would like to clarify that my concern was not about expecting to “get straight through in the morning.” My concern was about repeated attempts throughout the day, including the afternoon, where calls either rang out or disconnected automatically.

Being asked to contact the practice and then being unable to do so is understandably frustrating. Patients are not expecting special treatment — simply reasonable accessibility, particularly when prompted to make contact.

I hope that moving forward the focus remains on improving accessibility rather than questioning patient expectations.

We always ask that feedback is specific, proportionate and measured.  Yours is all of these so we thank you for your feedback.  

Unfortunately WMP has had some long term sickness recently which has affected our reception activities significantly.  This may have meant calls were not being answered in our usual timely fashion and for this we apologise.  We are over the worst of this now, but it may take a little longer for us to reach full speed.  Appointment numbers however have not been affected and we are still operating at full capacity as with all practices in the UK.

There was also a problem with the call back function last month which meant some patients were not receiving one as requested.  This has now been addressed.  

With regards to the messaging patients are receiving, we are reviewing our practices to see whether we can give patients the message they need rather than a generic message to contact the practice.  Obviously we have to consider confidentiality and the effect the message may have on patients, but it is in everyone's interest to avoid a call if not necessary.  

Finally, if you do need to call the practice, we advice calling after 4pm as this tends to be our quieter time.  It still bemuses us that patients expect to get straight through to the practice in the morning when there are 20 other patients calling for an appointment at the same time.  

Thanks again for your helpful feedback.  

Regards
